decision: Admit or reject (honest-FAIL) the benchmark case 'single sphere rolling down an inclined plane' into the DEM case pool: does the existing TensorDEM rigid-body-on-incline capability (tensordem.rolling_resistance.simulate_sphere_on_incline) reproduce the classical rigid-body reference a = g sin(theta) / (1 + I/(m R^2)) and alpha = a / R within 2 % at theta = 15 deg in the no-slip regime, with the rolling-resistance branch of Ai et al. (2011) reproduced when mu_r > 0?

alternatives.primary: reuse the repository's existing single-sphere incline harness (no new solver): Cundall-Strack tangential contact with no-slip, semi-implicit Euler, CDT rolling-resistance branch of Ai et al. 2011; reference = closed-form rigid-body acceleration
alternatives.alternative_1: write a new minimal rigid-body integrator for the case (rejected: duplicates an existing verified capability, cost without information gain; see docs/dem3d_rolling_resistance.md)
alternatives.alternative_2: measure the instantaneous acceleration instead of the steady-window least-squares slope (rejected as the acceptance metric, reported as a diagnostic: the undamped tangential spring makes the instantaneous a(t) oscillate about the mean, so an instantaneous sample is not a state variable of the model; the slope of v(t) over many oscillation periods is)
alternatives.alternative_3: frictionless/sliding branch as the reference (rejected: outside the declared no-slip regime of this case)

hypothesis: At theta = 15 deg with mu = 0.9 well above the pure-rolling requirement (f/(mu N) = 0.085), the sphere rolls without macroscopic slip and both the translational acceleration fitted from v(t) and the angular acceleration fitted from omega(t) match the closed-form rigid-body values within 2 %, independent of contact stiffness k_n and converging under time-step refinement.

metrics.M1_a_translational: a_t = LS slope of v(t) over the steady window (t >= settle), m/s^2
metrics.M2_alpha_rotational: alpha = LS slope of omega(t) over the steady window, rad/s^2
metrics.M3_no_slip_consistency: |a_t + R alpha| / |a_t| (kinematic closure v + R omega = 0)
metrics.M4_slip_residual: rms of the contact slip velocity v + R omega over the steady window, m/s
metrics.M5_rolling_resistance_branch: a_t (mu_r = 0.1 case) vs g (sin t - mu_r cos t) / (1 + I/(m R^2))
metrics.M6_critical_angle: measured zero-acceleration angle vs arctan(mu_r) (sign test on a_t)

unit_of_analysis: one harness run (one parameter point, one deterministic seed-free integration); the reported value is the least-squares slope over the steady window of that run. The integration is deterministic, so run-to-run scatter is exactly zero and no repetitions are used for M1/M2; uncertainty comes instead from the time-step refinement sequence (M1/M2 vs dt).

baseline_and_control.analytic_baseline: closed-form a = g sin(theta)/(1 + I/(m R^2)) evaluated in-code from g, theta and the sphere inertia factor I/(m R^2) = 2/5 (no hand-typed constants)
baseline_and_control.negative_control_1: artificially inflate the friction demand by setting mu = 0.01 (< 0.051 required) -> the sphere must slip and the no-slip reference must be violated by a large margin (proves the acceptance test can fail)
baseline_and_control.negative_control_2: eta = 0 must be rejected/raise instead of silently returning a wrong acceleration
baseline_and_control.negative_control_3: a_wrong = g sin(theta) (no inertia correction, i.e. sliding-without-rotation limit) must be rejected by the 2 % gate, proving the gate discriminates 1/1.4 = 71.4 % error

thresholds_declared_before_production_ru.convergence: M1/M2 relative error must be non-increasing on the dt sequence 4e-5 -> 2e-5 -> 1e-5 -> 5e-6 (allow one non-monotone step of at most 1.5x the previous error, documented)
thresholds_declared_before_production_ru.stiffness_invariance: M1 spread over k_n in {5e4, 2e5, 8e5} N/m must be < 2 % (the reference does not contain k_n)
thresholds_declared_before_production_ru.stopping_rule: if the base point fails the 2 % gate, stop and file honest-FAIL with fail_stage; do not retune parameters to pass (no threshold tuning after seeing results)

controlled: sphere radius R = 0.01 m, density 900 kg/m^3 (ice), solid-sphere inertia I/(m R^2) = 0.4
sliding friction mu = 0.9, rolling resistance mu_r = 0.0 (case A) / 0.1 (case B)
normal damping gamma_n = 0 (clean contact, no normal oscillation), initial height at static equilibrium
time integration: semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler, fixed dt swept over the declared sequence
steady window: t >= 0.06 s of a 0.24 s run (>= 300 tangential-oscillation periods)
confounders_and_nuisances: undamped tangential spring: a(t) oscillates about the mean with amplitude mu-independent ~0.29 g sin theta; the LS slope is the correct estimator of the mean, an instantaneous sample is not
semi-implicit Euler is only first-order and weakly amplifies/attenuates the slip oscillator at dt/period ~ 0.04; visible only at the coarsest dt (reported)
tangential demand vs Coulomb cone: if mu were near 0.051 the case would sit on the rolling/sliding boundary (excluded by mu = 0.9)
no rolling resistance in case A means the model has no static branch; irrelevant here because the sphere never stops

environment.threads: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, torch.set_num_threads(1) for run-time determinism/reproducibility of wall clock
environment.compute: local (single core), total wall clock < 5 min, no cluster needed

analysis_plan: Per point: fit slopes over the declared steady mask, compute relative errors against the in-code analytic value, mark pass/fail at 2 %. Aggregate: table ref vs got per metric with error column; convergence table over dt; invariance table over k_n; two negative controls executed and required to fail. Outliers are not removed; missing points are reported as such. Correlation vs causation: the agreement is a verification against a closed-form law, not evidence about any physical material.

amendments.what: reference alpha sign convention corrected to alpha_ref = -a/R (harness convention v>0 down-slope, omega about +z, no-slip v+R*omega=0). Before the fix the acceptance gate reported a spurious 200% error for alpha.
amendments.kind: reference definition fix (not a threshold change; the 2% tolerance is unchanged)
amendments.evidence: docs/CASE-DEM-ROLLING-SINGLE-PARTICLE.md section 1, provenance of the same run

amendments.what: added two DIAGNOSTIC metrics, not acceptance criteria: (i) instantaneous-acceleration oscillation amplitude vs the closed-form amplitude f*g*sin(t)/(1+f); (ii) sliding-branch comparison for the mu=0.01 negative control.
amendments.kind: diagnostic added after seeing results; explicitly excluded from pass/fail (pass still decided by M1/M2/M3 only)
amendments.rationale: the first run showed that the mean acceleration is exact at every dt while the instantaneous amplitude is the first-order-converged quantity; leaving that unquantified would overstate the model's instantaneous accuracy

amendments.what: runtime defect found while sizing the case: per-step cost in simulate_sphere_on_incline grew with step count (list-of-tensors history). Fixed by preallocating the history buffers; measured 5.8 -> 0.637 ms/step at 12k steps, results unchanged (54 existing rolling tests still pass).
amendments.kind: defect_fix in src (not a physics change)
